# Implementation Plan: AgentCMS Admin Portal

**Branch**: `001-admin-portal` | **Date**: February 13, 2026 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-admin-portal/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command following the workflow in `.specify/templates/commands/plan.md`.

## Summary

Build a React-based administrative portal for AgentCMS that enables content managers to create/edit/publish web pages, manage sites, and upload assets. The solution uses React 18 + TypeScript with TanStack Query for server state management, integrating with the existing .NET/C# REST API. Pages use a simple isPublished boolean flag (no scheduled publishing). Assets are managed independently (no page-asset associations). Targets <3s p95 page load times, WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility, and 90% first-time task completion rate.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.3+, React 18.2+  
**Primary Dependencies**: TanStack Query (server state), React Router (navigation), Zod (validation), Vite (build)  
**Storage**: Backend API (.NET/C#) with existing database - frontend consumes REST endpoints  
**Testing**: Vitest (unit), React Testing Library (component), Playwright (E2E), axe-core (accessibility)  
**Target Platform**: Modern web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge - latest 2 versions)
**Project Type**: web (frontend only - single-page application)  
**Performance Goals**: p95 page load <3 seconds, action feedback <2 seconds, 90% first-time task completion  
**Constraints**: WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance, file upload validation client-side before submission, optimistic UI updates, simple boolean publish flag (no scheduled publishing)  
**Scale/Scope**: ~10-50 content managers, 100s-1000s of pages per site, assets up to 10MB each, independent asset library (no page-asset associations)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

The AgentCMS Constitution (`.specify/memory/constitution.md`) requires that all features demonstrate adherence to five core principles:

### 1. Reliability ✓

**Durability & Recovery**: 
- All content edits use optimistic updates with automatic rollback on API failure
- Draft state persisted server-side - users can reload browser without losing work
- File uploads include client-side validation before submission (size, type, malware scan prep)
- Error boundaries prevent UI crashes from propagating

**Data Integrity**:
- Zod schema validation on all form inputs before API submission
- Backend API validates all mutations (frontend validation is UX enhancement only)
- Concurrent edit detection via `lastModified` timestamp comparison
- User warned if attempting to edit stale content

### 2. Consistency ✓

**UI Patterns**:
- Shared component library for forms, tables, modals, error states
- Standard toast notifications for success/error feedback
- Consistent keyboard navigation patterns (Tab order, Escape to close)
- Design system tokens for colors, spacing, typography

**Terminology**:
- "Site" (not "website/portal"), "Page" (not "document"), "Asset" (not "file/media")
- "Publish" for making content live (isPublished=true), "Draft" for work-in-progress (isPublished=false)
- No scheduled publishing - simple toggle between Published and Draft states

**Component Reuse**:
- `<FormField>` wrapper for all inputs (label, error, help text)
- `<DataTable>` for all list views (sites, pages, assets)
- `<ConfirmDialog>` for destructive actions
- `<FileUpload>` for asset management

### 3. Performance ✓

**Measurable Targets**:
- **Page Load**: <3s p95 for initial page render (Sites list, Pages list)
- **Action Feedback**: <2s for create/update/delete operations
- **Asset Upload**: Progress indicator for files >1MB, <5s for 10MB upload on typical connection
- **Search/Filter**: <500ms for client-side filtering, <2s for server-side search

**Optimization Strategies**:
- Code splitting via React.lazy() for each feature route
- TanStack Query caching reduces redundant API calls
- Virtualized lists for >50 items (react-virtual)
- Image thumbnails for asset previews (not full resolution)

### 4. Responsiveness ✓

**UX Feedback Mechanisms**:
- **Optimistic Updates**: Pages/Sites appear updated immediately, rollback if API fails
- **Progress Indicators**: Spinner for <2s operations, progress bar for uploads
- **Error Handling**: Toast notification + inline form errors with recovery actions
- **Loading States**: Skeleton screens for initial page load

**Interactive Latency**:
- Button click feedback <100ms (visual pressed state)
- Form validation on blur, debounced for expensive checks
- Autosave for page content every 30s (debounced while typing)

### 5. Maintainability ✓

**Modular Boundaries**:
- Feature-based structure: `src/features/{sites,pages,assets}` - each self-contained
- API client layer (`src/api/`) separates backend integration from UI
- Shared utilities (`src/lib/`) for validation, formatting, etc.
- Component library (`src/components/`) for reusable UI

**Testing Strategy**:
- **Unit Tests**: Zod schemas, utility functions, hooks (80% coverage target)
- **Component Tests**: React Testing Library for user interactions
- **E2E Tests**: Playwright for P1 user stories (create/publish page, upload asset)
- **Accessibility Tests**: axe-core integrated into component tests

**Documentation**:
- JSDoc for all exported functions/components
- README.md in each feature folder explaining domain logic
- API client methods documented with expected request/response shapes
- Storybook for component library visual documentation

### Post-Design Re-Evaluation

All constitution principles remain satisfied after Phase 1 design:
- **Reliability**: API contracts defined, error handling patterns documented in research.md
- **Consistency**: Data model enforces terminology, component reuse via quickstart.md scenarios
- **Performance**: Concrete metrics captured above, optimization strategies in research.md
- **Responsiveness**: Loading/error states specified in contracts/, optimistic updates in quickstart.md
- **Maintainability**: Project structure defined below, test scenarios in quickstart.md

**Structure Decision**: Web application (frontend only) with feature-based organization. Backend API exists separately (.NET/C# documented in `agentcms.api-swagger.json`). Frontend organized by domain features (sites, pages, assets) rather than technical layers, with shared components and API client as supporting infrastructure.

**Scope Simplifications**:
- **No publishedDate field**: Pages use simple isPublished boolean flag (no scheduled publishing)
- **No page-asset associations**: Assets managed independently in standalone library (no many-to-many relationship)
- **No backend dependencies**: Existing API already supports all requirements
